clue.text: Taking driver, for example, get ready to shoot birdie!

parts.note: a driver is a golf club of the kind traditionally called a wood
to cock a gun is to raise its hammer ready for firing

explanation.surface: A golfer reaches for the driver and lines up a birdie putt.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf words mislead: 'birdie' is not a score under par but a small bird, playfully named.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcock is a wading game bird, so it is a 'birdie' in the childish sense.

clue.text: Notable German wit on never missing victory in Europe

parts.note: a wag is a witty joker

indicators.note: the word never is shown without the letters for VE Day

parts.note: taken as written
VE stands for Victory in Europe, as in VE Day

explanation.surface: A famous German comedian never failed to joke about winning in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes VE from NEVER, leaving NER.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was a celebrated German composer.

clue.text: Finished scheme in debt

parts.note: something finished is over
a draft is a preliminary plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A finished scheme has left someone in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is money owed to a bank after drawing more than an account holds.

clue.text: Provide food for a couple of queens

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, giving CAT; ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth
a queen is a female cat, giving CAT; ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Someone is laying on a meal for two queens.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'queen' is both an adult female cat and, as ER (Elizabeth Regina), a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food and drink for an occasion.

clue.text: Single bishop in church leading song from 9

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
a side that is leading is up

explanation.surface: A lone bishop leads the singing in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is GREAT TIT; the answer is the chirping sound of a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirp or twitter is the short call of a small bird.

clue.text: Girl in fast car is a greedy person

indicators.note: the girl's name sits inside the letters for the sports car

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a fast touring car
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman in a sports car is accused of gluttony.
explanation.definitionFit: Gannet is informal British slang for a glutton, from the seabird's voracious feeding.

clue.text: Brigadier travelling on intercity flights

indicators.note: letters that travel move from their places, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An army officer takes flights between cities.
explanation.definitionFit: An airbridge is an air link carrying passengers or supplies by regular flights between places.

clue.text: Complaint over single girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a moan is a complaint
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A single girl makes a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a girl's name, from the Old Testament.

clue.text: Study over which Hoyle got worried?

indicators.note: worried letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: An academic subject that troubled Hoyle, the astronomer.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Hoyle was a British astronomer sceptical of religious accounts of creation, which gives the surface its joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Theology is the academic study of religion and God.

clue.text: European singer has a fantastic time with it

parts.note: fantastic means great
it is taken as written; 'with' links it on

explanation.surface: A European pop singer is having a wonderful time and is fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European singer' suggests a pop star; it is a songbird common across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tit is a songbird found throughout Europe, a singer in the bird sense.

clue.text: Love to annoy, welcoming old singer from America

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: one word takes the other in as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: to rile is to annoy

explanation.surface: Someone loves to irritate a visiting veteran American vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltimore oriole is a North American songbird, so a singer from that continent.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying unknown ruler

indicators.note: the vehicle word carries the other letter inside it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: A car carries an anonymous ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A czar, or tsar, was an emperor of Russia, a monarch.

clue.text: Duck down, for example

explanation.surface: A command to crouch, offered as an instance of ducking down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck down' reads as an order to crouch; split it into the bird and its soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sea duck, and its name also stands for the soft breast feathers it yields, as in eiderdown quilts.

clue.text: One might call for a sharp note!

definitions.text: One might call for a sharp note!

parts.words: One might call for a sharp note!
parts.note: read as a cutting bill or beak, a note being a bill, and also a bird whose name says it has a blade-like beak

explanation.surface: Someone demands a pointed note, perhaps a sharp musical tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp note' suggests music; a note is also a bill, and a bird's bill can be sharp as a razor. The bird has a cry, hence 'call'.
explanation.definitionFit: The razorbill is an auk named for its deep, blade-shaped beak, so a sharp bill indeed.

clue.text: Invented rumour of domestic employee at university

indicators.note: a rumour is something heard, so the word that follows is taken by its sound

parts.note: a maid is a domestic servant
in British usage a student is 'up' at university

explanation.surface: A false story is spread about a housemaid who went to university.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge is British idiom for being in residence at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fabricated or fictional is invented rather than true.

clue.text: Provides proof that vices need to be regulated

indicators.note: letters that must be regulated are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shows that vices need controlling.
explanation.definitionFit: To evidence something is to demonstrate or prove it.

clue.text: High flyer from faction on the extreme left

indicators.note: on here places the faction word after the colour word, joined onto its end

parts.note: red is the colour of the far left in politics
a wing is a faction within a party

explanation.surface: A rising star emerges from the hard-left faction of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High flyer' suggests an ambitious politician; it is literally a bird, a kind of thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: The redwing is a thrush, a bird and so something that flies high.

clue.text: I married one — a vet — it turns out to be not the real thing!

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: turning out the words shakes their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone marries a vet who proves to be a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges A VET IT into TATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imitative copies an original, so it is fake or derivative.

clue.text: Prisoner, female, soundly beaten in struggle

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is a prisoner

indicators.note: soundly here tells us to use the sound of the word beaten's synonym, not its spelling

parts.note: beaten means licked

explanation.surface: A female convict is thoroughly beaten in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' reads as 'thoroughly' but tells you to spell LICKED by its sound, LICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflict is a fight or clash, a struggle.

clue.text: Bird found on ring road with lots of money?

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O
ST is short for street, a road
having plenty of money means rich

explanation.surface: A bird turns up on a ring road, apparently wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the largest living bird.

clue.text: Church commission on drugs?

parts.note: one word that can come before Church and before Commission, and that also means intoxicated

explanation.surface: A church body investigates drug use.
explanation.walkthrough: The word combines with Church (Anglo-Catholic wing) and Commission (embassy between Commonwealth countries), and alone means intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: It forms High Church and High Commission, and on its own means intoxicated by narcotics.

clue.text: Cry comes back — it may be a consumer of 26!

indicators.note: coming back means the word for crying is read from right to left

parts.note: to cry is to weep
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cry returns; perhaps it is something that eats bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is INSECT; 'may be' marks the definition as a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing, also called this, feeds on insects and worms, so it eats bugs.

clue.text: Around six sheep getting frisky and irritable!

indicators.note: the rearranged animal letters go around the numeral
frisky animals jump about, so their letters are scrambled

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Around six o'clock the sheep become lively and bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: Shepherds call lively lambs and sheep frisky, which makes the anagram signal blend into the farmyard scene; the numeral is the clock time of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Peevish means easily annoyed or fretful.

clue.text: Make an offer for supply ship

explanation.surface: Someone bids for a vessel that carries supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To bid formally for a contract is one sense; the other is a boat that ferries stores to larger vessels.

clue.text: Feel a sigh escaping, seeing such a creature

indicators.note: letters escaping break loose from their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sigh of relief escapes someone on seeing a certain animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'such a creature' points back at the answer the letters make, a bird of prey that catches fish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large raptor that hunts fish, an animal of the kind described.

clue.text: The girl to go to court over silicon implant?

indicators.note: the chemical symbol is implanted inside the word for suing

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action
Si is the chemical symbol for silicon

explanation.surface: A woman sues over a silicone implant.
explanation.definitionFit: Susie is a girl's name, short for Susan.

clue.text: Runs into sponge rail!

indicators.note: one letter goes into the word for the cake

parts.note: a sponge is a light cake
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a sponge-cake on a railing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like a bar or railway; it is a family of marsh birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncrake belongs to the rail family of birds, so a crake is a kind of rail.

clue.text: Half of each beer is served up in a lobster claw!

indicators.note: half of the word each here means its second half
in a down clue, served up means the word is reversed upward

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: Half of each beer comes with a lobster claw.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue a word 'served up' is read bottom to top. 'Half of each' means the back two letters here, not the front pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A chela is the pincer of a crab or lobster.

clue.text: Bug new leader in international religious group

indicators.note: the leading letter is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

indicators.note: the leader of the word new is its first letter

explanation.surface: A new leader takes charge of a worldwide religious movement and causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug is a common informal word for any small creepy-crawly.

clue.text: Fried rib being cooked for 10

indicators.note: cooking food changes it, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A fried rib is cooked for ten people.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is ORIOLE; the Baltimore oriole has the nickname given here because of its flame-orange plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Firebird is a folk name in America for the orange-plumaged Baltimore oriole.

clue.text: Exam put back-she lacks heart to fly from Africa

indicators.note: putting it back reads the word for the exam in reverse

parts.note: a test is an exam

indicators.note: the word she loses its middle letter

explanation.surface: An exam is postponed because a student is heartbroken and must fly back from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns TEST into TSET; 'lacks heart' drops H from SHE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is a biting African fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Singer with passion has audience

parts.note: heat means passion, as in the heat of the moment
an ear is a hearing, an audience

explanation.surface: A passionate vocalist has listeners hanging on every note.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small songbird, so a singer.
